issue.title: Revisit true single-cargo-build packaging for the dev-update Rust install
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-i9.2 (epic sase-i9, 'Build the Rust core and LSP in one feature-unified cargo invocation') as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP. That phase's plan A was to collapse the two dev-update Rust builds into one cargo invocation whose feature-unified dependency graph both artifacts share, so sase_core compiles once per update instead of twice. Measured evidence recorded on sase-i9.2: a feature-unified 'cargo build --profile

-p sase_core_py -p sase_xprompt_lsp --features sase_core_py/extension-module' took 188.15s, and the following 'maturin develop' still rebuilt for 99.20s instead of only packaging. maturin 1.14 reruns 'cargo rustc' after the shared build, so the shared cache did not carry over. The phase therefore shipped the plan-B fallback documented in plans:202608/fast_dev_update.md: per-artifact CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolation ('/target/uv-tool-py' and 'target/uv-tool-lsp', Justfile recipes rust-dev-install / rust-dev-install-uv-tool). That stops the two builds from invalidating each other's cached units but still compiles sase_core twice on a core change, and costs a second target directory of disk. Scope: find out whether a newer maturin, 'maturin build --skip-auditwheel'/'--frozen', a hand-packaged wheel built from the shared target dir, or a maturin flag can make the packaging step reuse the feature-unified build's artifacts, and if so replace the target-dir isolation. Re-measure cold and warm 'just rust-dev-install-uv-tool' against the numbers above and against docs/rust_backend.md before switching. Lower priority now that the sase-i9.4 prebuild cache usually removes the compile from the interactive path entirely; this only helps runs that miss the cache.
